description: Manual corrections to the weekly supply-chain report that are not recorded elsewhere. Release tag pins live in release-tags.json and re-run weeks in the data branch; catalog exceptions in tools/*.json need an entry under catalog_exceptions; scan method changes go under method_changes (date of the first week scanned with the change, summary, pr or link); resolved finding disputes go under disputes (date, repository, advisory, optional package@version, status, summary, pr or link). Rendered at https://rezmoss.github.io/awesome-security-pipeline/corrections/.

method_changes.summary: npm development dependencies and npm-shrinkwrap.json are now scanned; matches on GitHub Actions referenced by a moving tag and on npm packages the repository defines itself are no longer counted; directories such as integration-tests and test-fixtures are excluded as fixtures. An OSV-Scanner confirmation now requires the same ecosystem, package, and version as the Grype match, not only the same advisory and package name (about 30 matches in the first 2026-11-02 run were confirmed by a different version); the list of advisories only OSV-Scanner reports is no longer cut at 100 per project. Advisories govulncheck finds in a release binary without a matching declared dependency (about 700 rows, mostly the Go standard library) now get advisory pages, CSV rows, and KEV and EPSS data, and count toward shipped advisories. Release verification reports build provenance, signature and signer, and release immutability separately; a release that is only immutable is no longer labelled verified (7 projects in the first 2026-11-02 run). Projects that left the catalog are excluded from current totals. The 2026-11-02 week was re-run with all of these changes; the first run is kept under runs/superseded/.

disputes.summary: govulncheck reports the Trivy supply-chain compromise (CVE-2026-33634, in CISA KEV) because the Go vulnerability database entry GO-2026-4919 lists every Trivy version from v0.69.4 on as affected, with no fixed version. The GitHub advisory for the same incident, GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23, lists only v0.69.4. kubescape v4.0.17 builds in v0.72.0.

entries.summary: The first week was published seven times by scheduled, manual, and push-triggered runs while the report pipeline was being finished. Each publish replaced the previous one without keeping it; every version remains in the supply-chain-data branch history. From 2026-11-08 only scheduled or explicitly dispatched runs publish, and a replaced run is kept under runs/superseded/.

A review of the first week found scanner errors, fixed from the week of 2026-11-02: two critical "Malware in ..." matches were false (salesforce/cloudsplaining's own npm package name and a local file: dependency in semgrep/semgrep matched malware published under the same names), four snyk/cli matches were on its own 1.0.0-monorepo workspace package, and 17 matches were on GitHub Actions referenced by a moving tag (v4, release/v1) that follows the latest, fixed release; npm development dependencies were omitted although the method includes them; npm-shrinkwrap.json was not read (AikidoSec/safe-chain showed 7 dependencies); and directories such as integration-tests, test-fixtures, and functional-tests were not excluded as fixtures. The 2026-11-01 data is unchanged; its "changes since last week" compared same-day re-runs and is now shown as a first scan.
